result: In 30 women with ME/CFS vs 25 controls, antihypothalamic (33%) and antipituitary (56%) antibodies were common, GH peak and IGF-1 were significantly lower, and both were lowest in the 13 high-titre patients, who were also more severe.
reason: Measures GH peak/IGF-1 directly and finds them low, adding an autoimmune subgroup and severity gradient to a contested finding; small sample.

result: ACTH and cortisol were significantly lower in 30 women with ME/CFS than 25 controls, most so in high-titre antipituitary/antihypothalamic antibody patients.
reason: Lower cortisol in the same direction, plus lower ACTH and an antibody subgroup suggesting a central (pituitary) mechanism.

result: In 106 ME/CFS vs 91 controls, shotgun metagenomics and qPCR showed fewer Faecalibacterium, Roseburia and Eubacterium, higher bacterial load, lower butyrate-synthesis capacity and lower fecal butyrate, with deficit correlating with fatigue.
reason: already cited: preprint of Guo 2023 (Cell Host Microbe), same 106 vs 91 cohort.

result: In short-term and long-term ME/CFS (79 long-term) vs 79 controls, gut diversity was lower and butyrate-biosynthesis genes, butyrate producers and plasma butyrate were reduced, especially in short-term patients.
reason: already cited: preprint of Xiong 2023 (Cell Host Microbe), same cohorts.

result: Short-term ME/CFS showed more microbial dysbiosis, while long-term (>10 y, n=79) ME/CFS showed more severe phenotypic and metabolic abnormalities.
reason: already cited: preprint of Xiong 2023, the sole study behind this finding.

result: 7T MRS of anterior cingulate in 22 CFS vs 13 controls found lower glutathione, total creatine and myo-inositol (water reference), but only myo-inositol stayed lower with NAA as reference.
reason: Finding claims glutamate/Glx changes, which this paper does not report; lower brain glutathione matches omics-redox, though it did not survive NAA referencing in a pilot sample.

result: In 20 ME/CFS vs 20 controls, resting time-domain HRV was normal while frequency-domain measures suggested reduced (para)sympathetic activity, and parasympathetic reactivation after an exercise bout was reduced.
reason: Same vagal-tone mechanism, adds the post-exercise recovery phase; resting time-domain null is a partial caveat; small study.

result: Central sensitisation (enhanced temporal summation plus inefficient conditioned pain modulation) was present in 16/19 (84%) CFS, 18/19 (95%) FM and 0/20 controls, excluding other pain disorders and centrally acting drugs.
reason: Independent cohort with QST showing impaired CPM in CFS, same direction; separate FM group partly addresses confounding.

result: Central sensitisation by QST was present in 84% of CFS, 95% of FM and no controls.
reason: Genetic-correlation finding; this is a phenotypic QST study with no genetic measures. Its correct link (neuro-pain-modulation-exercise-hyperalgesia) is already in this batch.

result: In 50 ME/CFS vs 50 controls (half male), females had lower total PE, arachidonic-PE and hexosylceramides, males had higher HexCer, MUFA-PE, PI, saturated TG and linoleic-derived oxylipins, and PC-dominated components correlated negatively with headache and fatigue severity.
reason: Does not report group differences in plasmalogens, PCs or sphingomyelins; reports sex-specific PE/HexCer/TG/oxylipin changes that no atlas finding covers (possible new omics item).
